clue.text: Elton John, for example, gets a rousing hand back East

indicators.note: rousing means stirring up, so the letters of gets a are stirred into a new order
back tells us the word for hand is read from right to left

parts.note: a hand is a worker, a man
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A singer receives an enthusiastic round of applause on returning to the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rousing' looks like describing enthusiastic applause, but it is the signal to rearrange 'gets a'; 'back' reverses the worker, and 'hand' is a labourer, not applause.
explanation.definitionFit: Elton John is the professional alias adopted by Reginald Dwight, an example of a performer's alias.

clue.text: Hardy girl, holding top of roan's mane

indicators.note: holding means the girl's name wraps around the letter that follows

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's heroine

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of the word roan's

explanation.surface: A tough girl grips the topmost hair on a roan horse's neck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' looks like the adjective tough; it is the novelist Thomas Hardy.
explanation.definitionFit: A mane is a head of long flowing hair, and a lock or curl of such hair is a synonym.

clue.text: Trees conceal old track

indicators.note: conceal means the trees surround and hide the letter for old

parts.note: a grove is a small group of trees

explanation.surface: Woodland hides an ancient path.
explanation.definitionFit: A groove is a long narrow channel or rut, a synonym for a track such as a record's spiral.

clue.text: Egg with touches of red in centre becomes kind of acid

parts.note: a nit is the egg of a louse

indicators.note: touches of means just the first light contact of each word, their initial letters

explanation.surface: A cooked egg with a reddish middle turns sour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becomes' is a link word; the initials come from red, in and centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitric acid is a strong corrosive acid of nitrogen, so the word names one type of acid.

clue.text: A second tea or coffee

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second, as in wait a mo
cha (char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: An offer of another cup: tea or coffee?
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a fine variety of coffee, originally shipped from the port of Mocha in Yemen.

clue.text: Bury the hatchet and skis splashed with paint

indicators.note: splashed means the letters of skis are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: with means and, joining things together
paint is slang for cosmetics, make-up

explanation.surface: Make peace, and daub the skis with paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms for ending a quarrel and becoming friends again.

clue.text: They take off more points as boxer finally reels

indicators.note: reels means staggers dizzily, so all these letters are jumbled together
finally picks the closing letter of the word boxer

explanation.surface: A boxer scores more points while his opponent staggers at the end of the bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reels' rearranges MOREPOINTSAS plus R, the last letter of boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: To take off someone is to mimic them, which is what professional mimics do.

clue.text: Investigators should go through with it

definitions.text: Investigators should go through with it

parts.words: Investigators should go through with it
parts.note: investigators go through evidence in minute detail, as if with a comb with close-set teeth

explanation.surface: Detectives ought to see the inquiry to its end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go through with it' reads as see it through; read literally it is combing through things.
explanation.definitionFit: To go through something with this tool is an idiom for examining it extremely thoroughly.

clue.text: Formal dress with fine diamond on film

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
rock is slang for a diamond
a film is a thin layer, a coat

explanation.surface: Evening wear with a lovely diamond, shown on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word placing the layer after the gem.
explanation.definitionFit: A frock coat is a man's knee-length formal jacket, an item of formal attire.

clue.text: Papers with small spread written up about ordinary characters with a message

parts.note: ID is identity papers

indicators.note: about means the reversed letters go around the letter for ordinary
written up in a down clue means the letters run from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
marge, short for margarine, is a spread
O is an abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: Documents with a little butter substitute are noted down, about ordinary letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written up' turns SMARGE into EGRAMS; 'about' places O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideograms are written symbols that stand for ideas, so they are characters carrying meaning.

clue.text: Ultimately swindler employs tricks

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so take the last letter of swindler

parts.note: to employ something is to use it

explanation.surface: In the end a con man resorts to deceptions.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruses are cunning stratagems or deceptions, synonymous with tricks as plural nouns.

clue.text: Australian poll's in the future

parts.note: poll is an old word for the head, as in poll tax

explanation.surface: An Australian opinion survey forecasts what is to come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poll' looks like a vote; it is the old word for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying before us in time, coming later, is an idiomatic sense of being in front.

clue.text: Hangman's craft?

parts.note: Jack ... was a notorious 17th-century English executioner, and his surname is also a type of two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: What skill does an executioner practise?
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like a trade or skill; it means a vessel, and Jack Ketch was a famous English hangman.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-masted sailing vessel shares its name with the executioner Jack Ketch, so it is his boat.

clue.text: Marine creatures run into prey

indicators.note: into means the letter for run goes inside the word for prey

parts.note: a kill is an animal killed as prey
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Sea animals dash at their quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: Krill are small shrimp-like crustaceans of the oceans, eaten by whales.

clue.text: Armoured vehicle not quite ready that follows Sierra

indicators.note: not quite means the word is cut short, dropping its final letter

parts.note: a tank is an armoured military vehicle
go means ready, as in all systems go

explanation.surface: A military vehicle is nearly ready to roll after a Sierra car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sierra' looks like the Ford car; in the NATO phonetic alphabet, Sierra (S) is followed by Tango (T).
explanation.definitionFit: In the radio alphabet the letter word after Sierra is this dance's name, standing for T.

clue.text: Oliver, say, is brave

definitions.meaning: Oliver ... was the larger half of the comedy duo Laurel and ...
brave in the sense of robust, bold and able to endure hardship

explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Hardy was a famous film comedian, and the word also means bold and tough.

clue.text: Northern Croat performing as singer

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters are acting out a new routine, a new order

explanation.surface: A Croat from the north appears on stage as a vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantor is the chief singer who leads the congregation in synagogue or church.

clue.text: American riots disturbed Duke for one

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters of riots are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Rioting in America upset a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A duke is a member of the nobility, an example of a toff in the informal short form.

clue.text: Private hotel on outskirts of Exeter

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel

indicators.note: outskirts of means the outermost letters of the word Exeter

explanation.surface: A secluded guesthouse on the edge of Exeter, a city in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private hotel' reads as one phrase, but 'Private' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner thoughts are personal and hidden from others, so the word means private or secret.

clue.text: Vocalist's token instrument

indicators.note: a vocalist's version of a word is how it is sung out, its sound

parts.note: a symbol is a token or emblem

explanation.surface: A singer's ceremonial musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A cymbal is a brass percussion plate struck in an orchestra, an example of a musical instrument.

clue.text: Finally digested 18's meal

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word digested

parts.note: the answer to 18 Across supplies the rest of the letters

explanation.surface: At last the food has been digested.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinner is the main meal of the day, eaten at midday or in the evening.

clue.text: John's vacuous poetry, a bit crazy

parts.note: john is slang for a lavatory, a loo; John's means John has

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so poetry loses all its middle letters

explanation.surface: John writes empty verse that is somewhat mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a poet's name; it is slang for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Loopy is informal for slightly mad or eccentric, a synonym of somewhat crazy.

clue.text: Not on reserve duty

parts.note: off is the opposite of on
ice means reserve, a cold aloofness of manner

explanation.surface: Off the reserve list and not on active service.
explanation.definitionFit: An office is a duty or function assigned to someone, as in the office of a priest.

clue.text: Work out with energy, taking time to produce a heavenly body

parts.note: to work out a scheme is to plan it
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An exercise session with energy, taking time, produces a gorgeous physique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavenly body' looks like a fit figure after the workout; it is a celestial one.
explanation.definitionFit: A planet is a large body orbiting a star, an example of a celestial object.

clue.text: Nearly naked ladette's beginning to wreck joint

indicators.note: to wreck is to smash apart, so the letters are rearranged
nearly means almost the whole word, so its last letter goes
beginning picks the first letter of the word ladette's

explanation.surface: An almost naked young woman is out to ruin a night spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' leaves NAKE; with L, 'wreck' rearranges NAKEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the hinge connecting foot and leg, an example of a bodily articulation.

clue.text: Follow, without question, Queen as ruler on a regular basis

indicators.note: without means the letter for question is removed
on a regular basis means every other letter of Queen as ruler

explanation.surface: Obey unquestioningly, with the Queen ruling as normal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on a regular basis' takes QENSUE from Queen as ruler; 'without' drops Q.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come after or happen as a result, an intransitive synonym of follow.

clue.text: Carry money, a respected thing

parts.note: to tote is to carry
M is an abbreviation for money, as in M1 and M3 supply

explanation.surface: Bringing cash is something to be admired.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem or object revered by a group, so it is a venerated symbol.

clue.text: Swap diamonds for clubs in outline

indicators.note: diamonds for clubs means the diamonds letter takes the place of the clubs letter

parts.note: to trace is to draw the outline of something
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A card player exchanges diamonds for clubs in general terms.
explanation.definitionFit: To trade is to exchange one thing for another, the same as to swap.

clue.text: Inquire as to name changes by electronic form for use in statistical comparison

definitions.text: form for use in statistical comparison

indicators.note: changes means the letters alter their order

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: Ask whether a name alters on an online form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges INQUIREASTO plus N, before E.
explanation.definitionFit: A questionnaire is a printed list of questions whose answers are compiled into statistics.

clue.text: They remind one of some English men on tour around capital of Trinidad

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters go around the letter that follows
on tour means travelling about, so these letters wander into a new order
capital of means the first letter of Trinidad

explanation.surface: Some English cricketers touring the Caribbean around Trinidad's capital collect souvenirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on tour' rearranges SOMEEMEN; 'around' puts T inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Mementoes are keepsakes or souvenirs kept to bring back memories of people and events.
